## 固定收益開場論點

7月30日美債收盤延續Fed會議後的政策可信度衝擊，走勢是盤整而非逆轉。2年期、5年期、10年期與30年期殖利率均上升1個基點，分別收在4.23%、4.38%、4.68%與5.21%。因此，2s10s與2s30s殖利率曲線在前一交易日異常大幅陡峭化後，維持在45與98個基點。相較7月29日，這些高檔水準得以持穩才是重要變化：長端殖利率不再加速逼近盤中極值，但油價走弱與英國利率的鴿派重新定價，都未帶來足夠買盤，使30年期殖利率脫離19年高點區域。

美國數據同時呈現當前通膨降溫與名目經濟承載力穩健的張力。第2季GDP年化成長率放緩至1.5%，但消費支出增加3.2%、國內私人購買者最終銷售成長3.9%，非住宅固定投資則增加8.4%。6月PCE物價月減0.1%，年增率由4.1%降至3.7%，但通膨降溫之際，實質消費仍增加0.4%，初領失業救濟金人數也維持低檔。因此，市場幾乎沒有理由將可能的政策反應提前，也缺乏依據排除陡峭曲線所反映的長期通膨與資本報酬風險。

Fed主席Kevin Warsh表示可能考慮PCE以外的指標，使下次升息時點未定之外，又增添第二層可信度問題。擴大分析範圍最終或可讓反應函數更清楚，但在未指定衡量指標的情況下，市場更難把2%承諾對應至政策。10年期實質殖利率持平於2.41%，10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點至2.27%，30年期實質殖利率也持平於2.98%。單日變動不大；但PCE物價月減後，實質殖利率與通膨補償仍居高不下，意義並不小。

信用市場將整體風險偏好與融資紀律清楚區隔。LQD上漲0.18%，兩檔大型高收益債基金約漲0.29%，S&P 500與Nasdaq 100則反彈1.66%與3.36%。儘管如此，CoreWeave仍須以基準利率加550個基點為其$26億貸款定價，較原訂區間上緣高出100個基點，才吸引約$90億訂單。Proofpoint在加強債權人保障並把利差提高150個基點後，才完成大部分展期；Fitch統計的私募信貸違約率則升至歷史新高6%。流動性仍在，但成交條件持續把經濟利益與控制權轉向貸方。

全球利率帶來的是相互抵銷的力量，而非一致的存續期間多頭行情。英國央行維持利率不變，並明確否定即將升息的看法，帶動2年期英國公債殖利率下跌11個基點，但長天期英債表現落後。歐元區成長優於預期，保留ECB再次升息的理由；日本則在BOJ決策前進場支撐日圓，而此前疲弱的2年期標售已顯露緊縮壓力。美元下跌0.73%，減輕一項外部制約，但長存續期間新興市場主權債指數仍下跌0.79%。因此，這次收盤並非普遍的融資斷裂，而是長存續期間成本高昂、各地政策選擇性紓壓，且信用承接愈加挑剔的市場環境。

## 美債殖利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

各附息券期別殖利率近乎平行上升1個基點，掩蓋了一項重要的不對稱。2年期殖利率報4.23%，較會後收盤高1個基點，但較一週前低14個基點。30年期殖利率報5.21%，一週上升4個基點，一個月上升35個基點。7月30日曲線未進一步陡峭化，但2s30s仍完整維持98個基點斜率；投資人撤除立即升息溢價，同時提高對較遠期通膨、財政供給與政策不確定性所要求的補償。

數據未能化解不同期限之間的分歧。GDP整體成長1.5%，淨出口拖累1個百分點，庫存再拖累0.67個百分點。基礎需求強得多：國內私人最終銷售成長3.9%，超過第1季增速的兩倍，也是2023年初以來最快。消費支出增加3.2%，工業設備投資更創2011年以來最大增幅。因此，疲弱的總體成長率並不代表經濟需要降息，尤其資本形成仍可支撐高報酬與融資需求。

通膨確實提供反向證據，但並不完整。6月PCE物價指數下降0.1%，年增率由4.1%放緩至3.7%，核心指標增幅也低於預期。實質消費支出仍增加0.4%，追平2025年7月以來最強單月增幅，儲蓄率則降至2022年以來最低。Fed在解釋耐心等待時，可以援引當前通膨降溫，但消費緩衝正在耗盡，7月能源價格也已高於6月。這種組合支持等待更多數據，卻不足以證實通膨風險溢價會持續回落。

市場定價只是把下一次政策決定延後，並未排除緊縮。交換市場給予9月升息25個基點約三分之二的機率，低於7月維持利率不變前的完全定價；年底前第二次升息機率則降至約40%。前端反映了這項延後。決策公布後，8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量減少約14萬口，先前超過100萬口的歷史高位部位開始退場。這只是事件尾端風險落地後的機械性部位出清，不代表市場已轉向寬鬆路徑。

Warsh的溝通使較長期預期更缺乏錨定。他重申2%目標，但表示正考慮比PCE更廣泛的通膨衡量指標，也未說明1月之後的架構可能如何調整。CPI同時也是TIPS的指數化依據，6月年增率為3.5%。在沒有明確替代指標或選擇規則下，投資人無從判斷較低的指標是否會延後行動，或更廣泛的一組指標是否會提高宣布抗通膨勝利的門檻。即使隔夜利率最終上升，這種模糊性也應反映在期限溢價與通膨風險溢價之中。

通膨連結債定價呈現了這項區別。10年期名目殖利率上升1個基點，實質殖利率維持2.41%，推升損益兩平通膨率至2.27%。長端方面，30年期實質殖利率維持2.98%，較一個月前高30個基點；30年期損益兩平通膨率則在Fed會後跳升後，處於約2.23%。最新交易日未重演週三的急劇重新定價，但PCE物價月減後也未能扭轉該走勢。TIPS交易活躍，按面額計成交$416億，較前一日增加22%，顯示市場高度聚焦通膨風險，但無法據此判定最終投資人的買賣方向。

現券交易也顯示，高檔收盤並非局限於曲線上交投清淡的一隅。名目附息券總成交額達$1.14兆，整體與前一交易日幾乎持平。20年以上期別面額成交增加17.8%，10年至20年區間增加37.5%，5年至7年區間則減少29%。成交集中方向與市場對長期前景的爭論一致，但雙向交易量無法辨識買賣方向。可以確定的是，30年期美債5.21%的收盤水準經歷大量價格發現後仍守得住。

供給目前仍是預期性溢價，而非已實現的標售結論。投資人正等待8月至10月再融資公告，市場預期附息券規模維持不變，但可能透過前瞻指引為明年增發預作準備。結構性疑慮在於，即使短期通膨放緩，強勁民間需求與龐大公共融資需求仍可能要求更高的均衡殖利率。以10年期殖利率接近4.80%、30年期殖利率約5.3%為目標價位的選擇權部位，顯示投資人願意為行情再次延伸支付溢價。本交易日的結論是殖利率在限制性水準盤整：事件風險退出前端，但長天期實質殖利率與財政供給的期限溢價並未獲得同等紓解。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

股市上漲帶動整體信用市場溫和復甦，但未消除本月由存續期間造成的跌價損失。LQD上漲0.18%、HYG上漲0.29%、JNK上漲0.28%。長天期AAA至A級與BBB級公司債指數分別上漲0.21%與0.26%，同時20年以上美債指數下跌0.09%。這些報酬顯示各信用評等的單日承接改善，並非可衡量的現券利差變動。以一個月來看，同一批長天期公司債指數仍下跌4.76%與4.38%，長存續期間融資成本依舊是信用環境的核心。投資人因而縮短信用品存續期間，而非放棄收益。過去一個月，剩餘到期日不到1年的歐元公司債報酬大致持平，整體指數下跌0.9%，10年以上期別跌幅則超過2.9%。3年期與9年期殖利率僅相差67個基點，利差又接近2008年以來低點，額外收益未必足以補償較高的利率與利差存續期間。這項配置訊號是選擇較接近到期的高品質收益，而不是信用風險已經消失。

CoreWeave提供了最具影響力且已完成的初級市場檢驗。其$26億延遲動用貸款以基準利率加550個基點定價，原始區間為加425至450個基點；相較該區間上緣，每年利息支出約增加$3,000萬。最終約$90億訂單承接這筆交易。這是一次成功配置，但前提是借款人大幅讓利，因投資人重新評估AI債務規模，以及在合約需求成熟前即融資擴充產能的風險。

這筆貸款的結構說明，成交水準為何比訂單簿本身更具資訊含量。貸款以晶片與客戶合約作擔保，包括與Anthropic及Jane Street簽訂的協議，評等為Ba2與BB+。本金會在5年貸款期間全數攤還；若承租人在找到替代客戶前未續約，CoreWeave須補足現金流缺口。然而，已簽約客戶合約的加權平均年期約3.1年，使貸方在貸款到期前承擔續約與使用率風險。初始合約約對應$40億營收，但抵押品品質並未消除期限錯配。

次級市場壓力使這項錯配更加昂貴。部分CoreWeave債券在本週動盪期間跌破90美分，殖利率一度落在13%區域，週四才告回升。其票面利率8.5%至9.75%的公司非投資等級債仍低於面額，殖利率約11%至12%。3月一筆由Meta合約支持的融資取得投資等級評等，並以基準利率加約225個基點定價。最新交易的利差遠為寬闊，顯示投資人正在區分客戶品質、合約期限與追索權，而非不分風險地拒絕所有晶片擔保結構。

Proofpoint也化解了另一項先前的不確定性，條件同樣有利於貸方。原擬$50億再融資中，$43億展延兩年，另有$7.35億仍於2028年到期。展延債務以基準利率加450個基點定價，原有融資則為加300個基點。債權人也取得阻止抵押品移轉的全方位限制條款、未來回購要約中的同等待遇，以及約二十餘項條款修訂。交易已確定到期結構與成本：融資管道得以保留，但2028年仍留有可觀到期餘額，利差也明顯提高。

這筆交易顯示，軟體業更廣泛的問題同時來自營運不確定性與資本結構。約$3,000億美國槓桿貸款將於2028年到期，近三分之一屬科技公司，其中許多在2021年併購週期中取得融資。AI衝擊可能削弱營收預期，但債權人眼前更關切的是，再融資前私募股權出資人能否移轉資產或優待特定貸方。Proofpoint的執行顯示，只要定價提高且資產外流受到限制，投資人願意延長存續期間。這不代表再融資到期牆已變得便宜，也不表示所有借款人都能達到相同的契約文件標準。

私募信貸提供了更具系統性的展期風險指標。Fitch追蹤1,300家美國私募債務借款人的過去12個月違約率，第2季由5.7%升至歷史新高6%。該機構記錄32起違約事件，涉及20家本期首度違約的借款人，其中逾半數包含到期日展延。工業與製造業違約率由5.9%升至10.4%，醫療保健則由6.9%升至9.4%。軟體業是重要例外，違約率由2.3%降至1.2%，顯示公開市場對AI曝險軟體業的憂慮，尚未造成同等程度的私募信貸已實現壓力。

其他融資管道仍然活躍，但同樣有選擇地移轉風險。法國興業銀行正規劃透過重大風險移轉交易，轉移約$50億專案融資貸款的風險。這類交易通常轉移投資組合5%至15%的第一損失曝險，支付給投資人的票息可超過10%；上半年SRT銷售超過$180億，高於一年前約$150億。法國興業銀行近期一筆交易，以基準利率加675個基點轉移逾90億歐元貸款的風險。銀行資本獲得釋放可維持新增放款，但也把資料中心與專案風險轉進要求兩位數補償的市場。

初級市場以外的債務管理手法同樣靈活。Xerox認列$1.05億關稅退稅應收款，並以$8,000萬現金出售，之後運用其中相當部分折價買回債務。該公司仍背負$42億債務，包括將於2028年8月到期的$5.56億無擔保票據。相較之下，Equinix在第2季資本支出增加60%至$15.8億後，宣布計畫發行至少$30億投資等級債券。澳洲AI基礎設施把同一項融資考驗進一步擴大：Blue Owl旗下Stack Infrastructure正為Melbourne專案尋求A$85億、約$59億聯貸；澳洲資料中心投資計畫總額估計超過A$1,550億，相當於GDP的5.6%。Stack也考慮出售位於澳洲、日本與馬來西亞、估值超過$300億的資產。連同CoreWeave，這些案例顯示融資市場涵蓋應收款變現、銀行資本風險移轉、資產循環運用，以及大額債券或貸款發行，但價格與結構愈來愈取決於存續期間、抵押品與未來現金流的確定性。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

英國央行帶來最明確的政策路徑紓壓。貨幣政策委員會以6比3票決定把銀行利率維持在3.75%，總裁Andrew Bailey並否定委員會正逐步走向升息的說法。2年期英國公債殖利率下跌11個基點至4.34%，9月升息機率由近60%降至40%以下。10年期殖利率僅下跌4個基點至4.99%，30年期則大致持平於5.73%。國內通膨降溫支撐前端，但量化緊縮與財政不確定性使長端溢價延續。

英國央行的情境分析明確指出能源依賴。基準路徑預估通膨將由2.6%升至2026年底3.2%的高峰，明年再回到接近2%。不利情境假設原油高於$100、天然氣價格上漲60%，使通膨高峰在2027年第2季升至4.5%；若衝突更快化解，高峰則限於3%。各情境下，英國2026年與2027年GDP成長率均維持在約1%。因此，英債為美債提供前端相對價值替代選擇，卻未形成明確的全球存續期間多頭行情：本地政策紓壓與集中在較長端的能源、資產負債表縮減及預算風險並存。

歐元區數據則朝相反方向發展。第2季GDP較前季成長0.4%，擺脫停滯，增幅是調查預估的兩倍，也是逾一年來最快。德國成長0.2%，第1季增幅上修至0.4%；法國在前季萎縮0.1%後成長0.2%；西班牙以0.7%表現領先。經濟活動展現韌性，即使能源衝擊抑制投資，也降低ECB再次升息的代價。因此，區域復甦使歐元前端殖利率對美債維持競爭力，也讓美國長端無法獲得各國政策同步寬鬆的推力。

日本同時面臨政策預期、標售疲弱與直接匯市行動。2年期JGB標售雖提供今年最高殖利率，需求仍弱於過去12個月平均。標售尾差由前月0.005擴大至0.007，債券期貨跌勢延續，2年期殖利率在1.47%附近交易，接近近期1.52%高點。隔夜交換市場反映9月升息機率約25%，10月前升息機率為79%。結果並不表示標售承接失敗，但確認在市場預期BOJ維持政策不變的會議前，買方要求較高的前端殖利率。

日圓盤中急升隨後改變跨境傳導。據一名了解相關行動的市場人士表示，日本進場干預以支撐日圓；日圓在紐約一度上漲3.3%，創2023年12月以來最大盤中漲幅。美國財政部長Scott Bessent表示，日圓遭到嚴重低估，過度波動並不健康。日本前一季已動用創紀錄的11.73兆日圓買進本國貨幣。干預可以緩解輸入性通膨，但若資金來自處分外國證券，便可能把匯市干預與全球主權債買方基礎連結起來。

中國債市提供防禦性存續期間的反例，而非全球共同寬鬆。第2季經濟成長率降至4.3%，低於官方4.5%至5%的目標區間，10年期公債殖利率因而降向1.7%，30年期公債期貨升至去年11月以來最高。政府承諾加快公共支出與債券資金運用；估計下半年未使用額度較去年多CNY1.3兆，但政策力度仍不及投資人期待。油價上升也使許多經濟學家撤回今年降息預測。對美債的淨影響有多有空，但仍偏限制性。由於國內通膨壓力看來較不持久，英國前端殖利率下跌；歐元區成長與日本政策預期則支撐較高的本地報酬門檻。全球資產管理人也開始直接交易這項分歧：Schroders增加美債空頭，同時買進澳洲、英國與歐元區前端公債；其他投資人則偏好澳洲、南韓、新加坡、挪威或中國公債，而非美國長存續期間部位。過去3個月，30年期美債殖利率上升約27個基點，同天期澳洲公債與英國公債則分別僅上升9個基點與7個基點。日圓突然走強也使美國短天期殖利率盤中下滑，並擴大美元跌勢，但30年期美債殖利率仍收在5.21%。海外發展與替代配置緩和了美國眼前的政策傳導，卻未帶動市場廣泛買進美元長存續期間資產。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場資產在美元走弱與長存續期間融資昂貴之間分化。美元指數下跌0.73%至100.07，EMB上漲0.24%。然而，15年以上新興市場美元主權債指數仍下跌0.79%，一個月跌幅達4.48%。這項分歧顯示，共同制約來自長天期美債折現率，而非普遍的美元流動性短缺。美元走弱支撐廣泛資產價格，卻無法補償持有最長天期硬通貨主權債現金流的投資人。

Danantara直接呈現這條傳導路徑。美債大跌後，投資人要求的殖利率高於其願意支付的水準，印尼主權財富基金因此延後推進原擬發行的20年期與30年期美元票據。該基金上月才透過5年期與10年期票據籌得$15億，因此這項變化並非融資管道完全關閉，而是在原定價格條件下，長天期市場暫時關閉；市場對這家年輕機構的治理，以及印尼盾兌美元近8%的跌幅，也加重了疑慮。

此案也延續市場先前對印尼政策可信度的擔憂。印尼央行總裁辭職，早已引發外界對機構獨立性與外部穩定的疑問。對一家管理約$9,000億國有資產的基金而言，成功發行長天期債券有助建立獨立於現任政府的機構定位。等待可保留定價彈性，但亞洲原已清淡的美元發行日程也因而缺少一筆指標交易，無法證明20年期與30年期新興市場供給可在當前美債殖利率附近順利成交。

肯亞考慮發行熊貓債，顯示其以不同方式回應同一項美元成本問題。政府正考慮在年底前發行約$3億等值的人民幣債券，以協助支應預估占GDP比重將由6.7%降至5.5%的財政赤字。今年發行的人民幣主權債與公司債殖利率約2.17%，不到新興市場美元債利率的一半。肯亞外債逾半數以美元計價，人民幣占12%；該國也已把約$31億鐵路貸款轉換為人民幣。分散幣別可降低換匯成本，但只是改變幣別組成，並未消除財政與償債風險。

馬來西亞則提供韌性的反例。外國投資人在7月淨賣出$14億馬來西亞債券，為2024年10月以來最大流出，但自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，其10年期殖利率僅上升22個基點，遠低於印尼與南韓至少80個基點的升幅。第2季GDP成長率由5.4%加速至5.8%，6月通膨則降至1.9%，馬來西亞國家銀行政策利率維持2.75%。預估占GDP 3.6%的財政赤字，也僅略高於3.5%目標。因此，相較共同的能源衝擊，本地通膨、財政可信度與成熟的國內買方基礎更為重要。

烏克蘭顯示，當全球投資人爭論其他央行是否延後行動時，本地政策仍可能轉向緊縮。烏克蘭央行意外升息50個基點至15.5%，推翻先前利率可能維持15%至2027年第2季的指引，並未排除今年再升至16%。官員預估年底整體通膨率為10%、核心通膨率為9.2%，並把戰爭列為主要風險；同時，IMF撥付近$7億款項，全年直接預算支援預計約$540億，補足了融資需求。新興市場的結論是融資選擇與政策反應分化，而非美元走弱帶來一致紓壓。馬來西亞能在殖利率僅小幅受損下吸收資金外流；肯亞探索人民幣融資，以降低對昂貴美元的依賴；美國存續期間重新定價後，Danantara延後發行長天期債券；烏克蘭則提高本地政策門檻以對抗通膨再起。全球共同因子決定硬通貨長天期融資成本；機構可信度、幣別組成、安全情勢與本地通膨則決定借款人能否改變融資管道，或只能等待。

## 跨資產

股市走勢否定前一交易日的廣泛緊縮訊號，但反彈集中於特定板塊。S&P 500上漲1.66%、Nasdaq 100上漲3.36%、半導體指數大漲8.19%，VIX則下跌17.28%至17.09。反彈幅度足以顯示，5.21%的長債殖利率尚未引發全市場去槓桿，但科技股修正並未消失：半導體指數一週仍下跌8.43%，一個月跌幅為17.55%。因此，股市反應改善風險偏好，卻未解決AI相關信用資產所隱含的融資與報酬疑問。

商品與匯市延續通膨與政策可信度之間的張力。WTI下跌0.56%至$83.99，Brent下跌1.50%至$89.38，緩和週三反彈後的當日能源推力。美元下跌0.73%，部分源於日圓干預加速其跌勢。儘管如此，黃金仍上漲3.29%至$4,167.40。油價走弱之際美債殖利率持穩，兩者並不衝突；但美元同時走弱、黃金買盤強勁，顯示投資人並未因PCE放緩而重拾對政策錨定的信心。

信用債基金跟隨股市上漲，但長天期新興市場主權債下跌，長天期美債也小幅收低。綜合訊號排除了無差別避險或普遍現金短缺，更支持範圍較窄的解讀：眼前波動與能源壓力緩解、科技股大幅回升、信用資產仍可交易，但長天期主權債折現率與未來通膨控制的可信度依舊偏緊。

## 前瞻市場意義

7月31日就業成本指數，以及下一批通膨與勞動數據，將決定國內需求展現韌性、Fed延後行動的組合，能否避免期限溢價再次上升。在國內私人最終銷售成長3.9%後，若薪資或物價證據仍然強勁，9月緊縮就仍會是可能選項；敏感的確認訊號將是2年期殖利率壓力重現，同時10年期損益兩平通膨率維持在會前區間之上。若要推翻目前解讀，勞動成本必須降溫、月度通膨持續下降，且實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率都要回落。8月至10月再融資公告則檢驗同一項長端溢價的供給面：附息券指引若維持不變，可消除眼前的公告風險；若為2027年擴大發行規模預作準備，30年期殖利率5.3%區域便會成為更可信的市場門檻。

日本央行7月31日決策必須在上月升息至1%、2年期標售疲弱，以及帶動日圓一度上漲3.3%的干預之間取得一致。若維持利率不變，但透過指引拉近下次升息時點，只要日圓維持強勢且JGB未再失序拋售，就能印證匯市干預。若訊息使10月升息的可能性下降，重複干預的負擔將加重，輸入性通膨壓力也可能再次升高。對美債的影響會透過相對殖利率與準備資產兩條路徑傳導：日本殖利率與匯率穩定，可降低全球期限溢價外溢；JGB報酬上升或進一步出售外國證券，則會限制長存續期間美債的邊際買盤。

下一批AI基礎設施與軟體業融資，將決定CoreWeave加550個基點的利差是新的成交水準，或只是對合約錯配的單筆交易反應。Equinix計畫發行至少$30億債券，加上後續以晶片或客戶合約擔保的貸款，最有資訊價值的不是能否定價，而是訂單簿深度、讓利、期限與債權人保障。若配置後需求仍穩定，次級市場殖利率也未再上升，壓力便可侷限於合約短或追索權弱的借款人。若需要額外折價、續約保證或抵押品阻擋條款，則代表CoreWeave的$90億訂單與Proofpoint展期，是透過重設整個產業的貸方經濟條件達成，而非恢復被動承接。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The July 30 Treasury close consolidated, rather than reversed, the policy-credibility shock delivered after the Fed meeting. The 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields each rose 1 basis point, to 4.23%, 4.38%, 4.68% and 5.21%. The 2s10s and 2s30s curves consequently held at 45 and 98 basis points after the prior session's exceptional steepening. Stability at those elevated levels is the important change from July 29: the long end stopped accelerating toward its intraday extremes, but neither softer oil nor a dovish repricing in UK rates restored demand sufficient to pull the 30-year yield away from a 19-year-high region.

The US data mix reinforced the tension between easing current inflation and resilient nominal capacity. Q2 GDP slowed to a 1.5% annualized rate, yet consumer spending rose 3.2%, final sales to private domestic purchasers advanced 3.9%, and nonresidential fixed investment increased 8.4%. June PCE prices fell 0.1% on the month and the annual rate eased to 3.7% from 4.1%, but that disinflation arrived alongside a 0.4% rise in real consumption and still-low jobless claims. The market therefore received little reason to bring the likely policy response forward, and little basis for dismissing the longer-run inflation and return-on-capital risk embedded in the steep curve.

Chairman Kevin Warsh's suggestion that the Fed could look beyond PCE added a second credibility problem to the uncertain timing of the next hike. A wider analytical lens may eventually clarify the reaction function, but the absence of specified metrics makes the 2% commitment harder to map into policy. The 10-year real yield was unchanged at 2.41% and the 10-year breakeven rose 1 basis point to 2.27%, while the 30-year real yield also held at 2.98%. The daily move was small; the persistence of elevated real yields and inflation compensation after a benign monthly PCE print was not.

Credit separated broad risk appetite from financing discipline. LQD gained 0.18% and the two large high-yield funds rose about 0.29%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rebounded 1.66% and 3.36%. CoreWeave nevertheless had to price its $2.6 billion loan at 550 basis points over the benchmark, 100 basis points above the top of its original range, before attracting about $9 billion of orders. Proofpoint completed most of its extension only after stronger creditor protections and a 150-basis-point increase in margin, while Fitch's private-credit default rate reached a record 6%. Liquidity remained available, but clearing terms continued to transfer economics and control toward lenders.

Global rates added offsets, not a common duration rally. The BOE's hold and explicit resistance to an imminent hike drove the 2-year gilt yield 11 basis points lower, even as long gilts lagged. Euro-area growth beat expectations, preserving the case for another ECB increase, and Japan intervened to support the yen before the BOJ decision after a weak 2-year auction had already exposed tightening pressure. A 0.73% dollar decline relieved one external constraint, yet the long-duration EM sovereign index fell 0.79%. The completed close was thus not a generalized funding break; it was a regime of expensive long duration, selective local policy relief and increasingly discriminating credit absorption.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The near-parallel 1-basis-point rise across coupon maturities belied an important asymmetry. At 4.23%, the 2-year yield remained 1 basis point above the post-meeting close and 14 basis points below its level a week earlier. The 30-year yield at 5.21% was 4 basis points higher over the week and 35 basis points higher over the month. The curve did not steepen further on July 30, but it retained the full 98-basis-point 2s30s slope created as investors removed the immediate-hike premium and raised the compensation required for inflation, fiscal supply and policy uncertainty farther out.

The data did not resolve that horizon split. Headline GDP growth of 1.5% was restrained by net exports, which subtracted 1 percentage point, and inventories, which removed another 0.67 percentage point. Underlying demand was much stronger: private domestic final sales grew 3.9%, more than twice the Q1 pace and the fastest since early 2023. Consumer spending rose 3.2%, and investment in industrial equipment posted its largest increase since 2011. A soft aggregate growth rate therefore did not describe an economy requiring rate relief, particularly when capital formation can sustain high returns and demand for financing.

Inflation offered genuine, but incomplete, counterevidence. The PCE price index fell 0.1% in June, its annual rate slowed to 3.7% from 4.1%, and the core measure rose less than forecast. Real consumer spending still increased 0.4%, matching the strongest monthly gain since July 2025, while the saving rate fell to its lowest since 2022. The Fed can point to current disinflation when explaining patience, but the consumption cushion is being depleted and July energy prices had already moved above June levels. That combination supports waiting for more data without validating a durable retreat in the inflation risk premium.

Market pricing shifted the next policy decision later rather than removing tightening. Swaps assigned roughly a two-in-three chance to a 25-basis-point September increase, down from a fully priced move before the July hold, and the probability of a second increase by year-end fell to about 40%. The front end reflected that delay. August fed-funds futures open interest dropped by roughly 140,000 contracts after the decision as a record position exceeding 1 million contracts began to unwind. This was the mechanical clearing of a realized event tail, not evidence that the market had adopted an easing path.

Warsh's communication left the longer horizon less anchored. He reaffirmed the 2% objective but said he was considering a broader set of inflation measures than PCE and left open what the framework might become after January. CPI, which is also the index used for TIPS, was running at 3.5% in June. Without a defined replacement metric or selection rule, investors cannot know whether a softer gauge would delay action or whether a broader set of measures would raise the hurdle for declaring victory. That ambiguity belongs in term and inflation-risk premiums even if the overnight rate ultimately rises.

Inflation-linked pricing captured the distinction. The 10-year nominal yield rose 1 basis point while the real yield stayed at 2.41%, lifting the breakeven to 2.27%. At the long end, the 30-year real yield remained 2.98%, 30 basis points above its month-earlier level, while the 30-year breakeven stood near 2.23% after the post-Fed jump. The latest session did not repeat Wednesday's abrupt repricing, but it also failed to unwind it after a monthly decline in PCE prices. TIPS activity was elevated, with $41.6 billion of par traded, 22% more than the previous day, consistent with concentrated attention on inflation risk without identifying the direction of end-investor flow.

Cash activity also showed that the elevated close was not confined to a quiet corner of the curve. Nominal-coupon trading totaled $1.14 trillion, almost unchanged from the prior session overall. Par activity rose 17.8% in maturities longer than 20 years and 37.5% in the 10-to-20-year sector, while the 5-to-7-year bucket fell 29%. The concentration aligned with the market's long-horizon debate, though two-way turnover cannot identify buying or selling. It does show that the 5.21% long-bond close survived substantial price discovery.

Supply remained an anticipatory premium rather than a realized auction verdict. Investors were looking toward the August-to-October refunding announcement, with coupon sizes expected to remain steady but the possibility of guidance preparing increases next year. The structural concern is that robust private demand and a large public financing need may require a higher equilibrium yield even if near-term inflation slows. Options seeking 10-year yields near 4.80% and 30-year yields around 5.3% showed where investors were paying for another extension. The session's conclusion was consolidation at restrictive levels: event risk left the front end, but no equivalent relief reached long real yields or the fiscal term premium.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit recovered modestly as equities rallied, without erasing the month's duration damage. LQD rose 0.18%, HYG gained 0.29%, and JNK added 0.28%. Long-maturity AAA-to-A and BBB corporate bond indices increased 0.21% and 0.26%, even as the 20-year-plus Treasury index slipped 0.09%. Those returns show better daily absorption across credit quality, not a measurable cash-spread move. Over 1 month, the same long corporate indices remained down 4.76% and 4.38%, keeping the cost of long-duration financing central to the credit regime. Investors were responding by shortening credit exposure rather than abandoning income: euro corporate bonds with less than 1 year to maturity were approximately flat over the prior month, compared with a 0.9% loss for the broad index and a decline exceeding 2.9% for maturities of at least 10 years. With only 67 basis points between 3- and 9-year yields and spreads near their tightest since 2008, the incremental carry did not compensate every buyer for the added rate and spread duration. The allocation signal was therefore quality income closer to redemption, not a claim that credit risk itself had disappeared.

CoreWeave supplied the most consequential completed primary-market test. Its $2.6 billion delayed-draw loan priced at 550 basis points over the benchmark, compared with an initial range of 425 to 450, increasing annual interest expense by about $30 million relative to the top of that range. Roughly $9 billion of orders ultimately covered the transaction. That is a successful placement, but only after the borrower paid a large concession as investors reassessed the volume of AI debt and the risk of financing capacity before contracted demand has matured.

The loan's structure explains why the clearing level carries more information than its orderbook alone. It is backed by chips and customer contracts, including agreements with Anthropic and Jane Street, and received Ba2 and BB+ ratings. Principal amortizes to zero over the five-year life, and CoreWeave guarantees cash-flow gaps if a tenant does not renew before a replacement is found. Yet the weighted average life of contracted customers is about 3.1 years, leaving lenders exposed to renewal and utilization risk before maturity. The initial contracts represent about $4 billion of revenue, but collateral quality did not eliminate the mismatch.

Secondary stress made that mismatch more expensive. Some CoreWeave bonds fell below 90 cents and briefly yielded in the 13% area during the week's upheaval before recovering on Thursday. Its corporate junk bonds, issued with 8.5% to 9.75% coupons, were still below par at roughly 11% to 12% yields. A March financing backed by Meta contracts achieved an investment-grade rating and priced about 225 basis points over the benchmark. The much wider spread on the latest transaction shows that investors are differentiating among customer quality, contract duration and recourse, not rejecting every chip-backed structure as one risk.

Proofpoint resolved another prior uncertainty, again on lender-favorable terms. Of the proposed $5 billion refinancing, $4.3 billion was extended by two years and $735 million remained due in 2028. The extended debt priced 450 basis points over the benchmark, versus 300 on the existing financing. Creditors also secured an omni blocker against collateral transfers, equal treatment in future repurchase offers and revisions to roughly two dozen provisions. The current delta is the completed allocation of maturity and cost: access was preserved, but a meaningful 2028 stub and materially higher margin remained.

The transaction locates the wider software problem in both operating uncertainty and capital structure. About $300 billion of US leveraged loans mature in 2028, nearly one-third of them for technology companies, many financed during the 2021 buyout cycle. AI disruption can weaken revenue expectations, yet the immediate creditor concern is whether sponsors can move assets or favor selected lenders before refinancing. Proofpoint's execution shows that investors will extend duration when pricing rises and leakage is constrained. It does not show that the refinancing wall has become cheaper or that all borrowers can meet the same documentary standard.

Private credit supplied a more systemic measure of extension risk. Fitch's trailing 12-month default rate across 1,300 US private-debt borrowers rose to a record 6% in Q2 from 5.7%. The agency recorded 32 default events involving 20 new unique defaulters, and more than half included maturity extensions. Industrials and manufacturing reached a 10.4% default rate, up from 5.9%, while healthcare rose to 9.4% from 6.9%. Software was an important exception at 1.2%, down from 2.3%, showing that public-market anxiety about AI-exposed software has not yet produced equivalent realized private-credit stress.

Other financing channels remained active, but they also transferred risk selectively. Societe Generale was preparing protection on about $5 billion of project-finance loans through a significant-risk-transfer transaction. Such deals typically shift first-loss exposure on 5% to 15% of a portfolio and can pay investors coupons above 10%; first-half SRT sales reached more than $18 billion, versus about $15 billion a year earlier. A recent SocGen transaction transferred risk on more than EUR9 billion of loans at 675 basis points over the benchmark. Bank capital relief can sustain origination, but it moves data-center and project risk into a market demanding double-digit compensation.

Debt management below the primary market was equally resourceful. Xerox recognized $105 million of tariff-refund receivables and sold them for $80 million in cash, then used a meaningful portion to repurchase debt at a discount. The company still carried $4.2 billion of debt, including $556 million of unsecured notes due in August 2028. Equinix, by contrast, announced plans for at least $3 billion of investment-grade bonds after Q2 capital expenditure rose 60% to $1.58 billion. Australian AI infrastructure broadened the same funding test: Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure was seeking an A$8.5 billion, or $5.9 billion, syndicated loan for a Melbourne project, while the country's data-center investment pipeline was estimated above A$155 billion, equal to 5.6% of GDP. Stack was also considering a sale of Australian, Japanese and Malaysian assets valued above $30 billion. Together with CoreWeave, the cases show a financing market spanning receivable monetization, bank-capital transfer, asset recycling and large bond or loan issuance, but with price and structure increasingly dictated by duration, collateral and the certainty of future cash flow.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

The BOE delivered the clearest policy-path relief. It held Bank Rate at 3.75% by a 6-3 vote, and Governor Andrew Bailey rejected the idea that the committee was edging toward a hike. The 2-year gilt yield fell 11 basis points to 4.34%, and the chance of a September increase dropped below 40% from almost 60%. Ten-year yields declined only 4 basis points to 4.99%, while the 30-year was little changed at 5.73%. Domestic disinflation supported the front end, but quantitative tightening and fiscal uncertainty preserved a long-end premium.

The BOE's scenarios made the energy dependency explicit. Its central path put inflation at a 3.2% peak late in 2026, from 2.6%, before a return toward 2% next year. An adverse case with crude above $100 and gas prices 60% higher lifted the peak to 4.5% in Q2 2027, whereas quicker conflict resolution limited it to 3%. GDP growth remained near 1% in 2026 and 2027 across the scenarios. Britain therefore offered Treasuries a front-end relative-value alternative, but not a clean global duration rally: local policy relief coexisted with energy, balance-sheet runoff and budget risks concentrated farther out.

Euro-area data moved in the opposite direction. Q2 GDP rose 0.4% from the prior quarter after stagnation, twice the survey estimate and the strongest growth in more than a year. Germany expanded 0.2% after Q1 was revised to 0.4%, France grew 0.2% after a 0.1% contraction, and Spain outperformed at 0.7%. Resilient activity reduces the cost of another ECB increase even as the energy shock curbs investment. The regional recovery therefore keeps euro front-end yields competitive with Treasuries and denies the US long end a synchronized foreign-policy easing impulse.

Japan combined policy anticipation, auction softness and direct currency action. The 2-year JGB auction drew weaker demand than its 12-month average despite offering the highest yield of the year. Its tail widened to 0.007 from 0.005 the prior month, bond futures extended losses, and the 2-year yield traded near 1.47%, close to its recent 1.52% peak. Overnight swaps assigned about 25% probability to a September increase and 79% by October. The result did not show failed absorption, but it confirmed that buyers required elevated front-end yields before a BOJ meeting expected to leave policy unchanged.

The yen's intraday surge then altered the cross-border channel. Japan intervened to support the currency, according to a market participant familiar with the action, and the yen advanced as much as 3.3% in New York, its largest intraday gain since December 2023. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the yen as very undervalued and excessive volatility as unhealthy. Japan had already spent a record JPY11.73 trillion on currency purchases in the previous quarter. Intervention can relieve imported inflation, but financing it through foreign-security holdings creates a potential link to the global sovereign buyer base.

China added a defensive-duration counterexample rather than a common easing impulse. Q2 growth slowed to 4.3%, below the 4.5% to 5% official target range, sending the 10-year government yield toward 1.7% and 30-year bond futures to their highest since November. Authorities pledged faster public spending and bond-fund deployment, with second-half unused quota estimated at CNY1.3 trillion more than the prior year, but stopped short of the stimulus investors had expected; higher oil prices had also caused many economists to withdraw calls for a rate cut. The net implication for Treasuries was mixed but still restrictive. UK front-end yields fell because domestic inflation pressure looked less persistent, while euro growth and Japanese policy expectations supported higher local return hurdles. Global managers were actively expressing the divergence: Schroders was adding bearish Treasury positions while buying front-end government bonds in Australia, the UK and euro area, and other investors favored Australia, South Korea, Singapore, Norway or Chinese government bonds over long US duration. Over 3 months, the 30-year Treasury yield had risen about 27 basis points, versus 9 basis points for its Australian counterpart and 7 basis points for comparable gilts. The sudden yen move also helped pull shorter US yields down intraday and extended the dollar's decline, yet the 30-year Treasury still closed at 5.21%. Foreign developments and allocation alternatives softened the immediate US policy channel without producing a broad bid for long dollar duration.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market assets split between softer dollar conditions and expensive long-duration funding. The Dollar Index fell 0.73% to 100.07, and EMB gained 0.24%. The 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index nevertheless lost 0.79% and was down 4.48% over 1 month. That divergence identifies the common constraint as the long Treasury discount rate rather than a broad shortage of dollar liquidity. A weaker dollar supported broad marks, but it could not compensate investors holding the longest hard-currency sovereign cash flows.

Danantara showed that transmission directly. Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund delayed progress on contemplated 20- and 30-year dollar notes because investors demanded more yield than it was willing to pay after the Treasury rout. The fund had raised $1.5 billion in five- and 10-year notes the previous month, so the change was not a complete loss of access. It was a maturity-specific closure at the proposed economics, compounded by concern about the young institution's governance and the rupiah's nearly 8% decline against the dollar.

The case also extended the prior concern over Indonesian policy credibility. The resignation of Bank Indonesia's governor had already raised questions about institutional independence and external stability. For a fund overseeing state assets valued at about $900 billion, successful long-dated issuance would help establish an identity independent of the current administration. Waiting preserves pricing flexibility, but it leaves Asia's subdued dollar calendar without a benchmark transaction capable of showing that 20- and 30-year EM supply can clear near current Treasury yields.

Kenya's contemplated panda bond illustrated a different response to the same dollar-cost problem. The government was considering a yuan-equivalent sale of about $300 million by year-end to help fund a deficit expected to narrow to 5.5% of GDP from 6.7%. Yuan sovereign and corporate bonds issued this year yielded about 2.17%, less than half the rate on EM dollar debt. More than half of Kenya's external debt is in dollars, against 12% in yuan, and it had already converted about $3.1 billion of railway loans into renminbi. Diversification can reduce conversion costs, though it changes the currency composition rather than removing fiscal and repayment risk.

Malaysia provided the resilience counterexample. Foreign investors sold a net $1.4 billion of Malaysian bonds in July, the largest outflow since October 2024, yet its 10-year yield had risen only 22 basis points since the Iran war began, compared with at least 80 basis points in Indonesia and South Korea. Q2 GDP growth accelerated to 5.8% from 5.4%, while June inflation eased to 1.9% and Bank Negara's rate remained 2.75%. A projected 3.6%-of-GDP deficit would be only slightly above the 3.5% target. Local inflation, fiscal credibility and an established domestic buyer base therefore mattered more than the common energy shock.

Ukraine demonstrated that domestic policy could tighten even while global investors debated delayed action elsewhere. The central bank unexpectedly raised its benchmark rate 50 basis points to 15.5%, reversing earlier guidance that 15% would probably hold until Q2 2027, and did not rule out 16% later in the year. Officials projected year-end headline inflation of 10% and core inflation of 9.2%, citing war as the principal risk, even as an IMF tranche of almost $700 million and expected direct budget support of about $54 billion covered the financing side. The EM conclusion was dispersion in funding choice and policy response, not uniform relief from a softer dollar. Malaysia could absorb outflows with limited yield damage, Kenya explored renminbi finance to reduce dependence on expensive dollars, Danantara postponed long-maturity issuance as US duration repriced, and Ukraine raised the local policy hurdle against renewed inflation. The common global factor set the cost of hard-currency tenor; institutional credibility, currency composition, security conditions and local inflation determined whether borrowers could alter the channel or had to wait.

## Cross asset

Equities rejected the prior session's broad tightening signal, but the rebound was concentrated. The S&P 500 rose 1.66%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 3.36%, and the semiconductor index surged 8.19%, while the VIX fell 17.28% to 17.09. That recovery was large enough to show that a 5.21% long-bond yield had not triggered economy-wide deleveraging. It did not erase the technology correction: the semiconductor index remained down 8.43% over 1 week and 17.55% over 1 month. The equity response therefore improved risk appetite without resolving the financing and return questions embedded in AI credit.

Commodities and currencies preserved the inflation-credibility tension. WTI declined 0.56% to $83.99 and Brent fell 1.50% to $89.38, reducing the same-session energy impulse after Wednesday's rebound. The dollar lost 0.73%, partly as yen intervention accelerated its decline. Gold nevertheless rose 3.29% to $4,167.40. Softer oil was compatible with stable Treasury yields, but simultaneous dollar weakness and a strong gold bid showed that investors had not converted the PCE slowdown into renewed confidence in the policy anchor.

Credit funds gained alongside equities, yet long EM sovereign bonds fell and long Treasuries were slightly negative. The combined signal rules out an indiscriminate flight from risk or a generalized cash shortage. It instead supports a narrower interpretation: immediate volatility and energy pressure eased, technology equities recovered sharply, and credit remained tradable, while long sovereign discount rates and confidence in future inflation control stayed restrictive.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 31 Employment Cost Index and the next inflation and labor releases determine whether resilient domestic demand can coexist with delayed Fed action without another rise in term premium. Wage or price evidence that remains firm after 3.9% growth in private domestic final sales would keep September tightening active; the sensitive confirmation would be renewed pressure in the 2-year yield alongside 10-year breakevens holding above the pre-meeting range. Softer labor costs and continued monthly disinflation need to lower both real yields and breakevens to overturn the current interpretation. The August-to-October refunding announcement tests the supply side of the same long-end premium: steady coupon guidance would remove an immediate announcement risk, whereas preparation for larger 2027 sizes would make the 5.3% area in the 30-year yield a more credible market threshold.

The Bank of Japan decision on July 31 must reconcile the prior month's increase to 1%, a weak 2-year auction and intervention that lifted the yen as much as 3.3%. A hold accompanied by guidance that brings the next increase closer can validate the currency action if the yen remains firmer without another disorderly JGB selloff. A message that leaves October tightening less likely would place more burden on repeated intervention and could renew imported-inflation pressure. The Treasury consequence runs through both relative yield and reserves: stable Japanese yields and currency reduce global term-premium spillover, while higher JGB returns or further foreign-security sales keep the marginal bid for long US duration constrained.

The next AI infrastructure and software financings determine whether CoreWeave's 550-basis-point margin is a new clearing level or a transaction-specific response to contract mismatch. Equinix's planned sale of at least $3 billion and subsequent chip- or customer-backed loans will be most informative through orderbook depth, concession, maturity and creditor protections, not merely whether they price. Demand that holds after allocation without another widening in secondary yields would contain the pressure to borrowers with short contracts or weak recourse. Additional discounts, renewal guarantees or collateral blockers would show that the $9 billion CoreWeave book and Proofpoint extension were achieved by resetting lender economics across the sector rather than by restoring passive absorption.
